claims.text: The selected high-entropy alloy has random chemical occupancy.
The selected alloy has a stable lattice framework.
The selected alloy has no superconducting energy gap above its expected transition temperature.
The selected alloy has no detectable local lattice distortions above its expected transition temperature.
Cooling toward the superconducting transition causes local lattice distortions to develop.
The cooling-induced local lattice distortions enhance electron-phonon coupling.
An isotropic s-wave superconducting gap emerges in the chemically disordered electronic structure.
On cooling, disordered atomic sites subtly reorganize and lessen local strain.
Reduced local strain enhances phonon coherence.
Enhanced phonon coherence and electron-phonon interactions foster conventional BCS-type s-wave pairing despite chemical disorder.
Below the transition temperature, ARPES should detect an isotropic superconducting gap relative to the high-temperature baseline.
Below the transition temperature, scattering should show local structural changes such as peak shifts or splitting.
The proposed mechanism should apply broadly to high-entropy alloys with similar chemical disorder and stable lattice frameworks under cryogenic, ambient-pressure conditions.
The proposed mechanism may fail in high-entropy alloys having extrinsic ordering or substantial non-equilibrium phases.
Analogous high-entropy alloy superconductors exhibit behavior consistent with conventional weak-coupling, isotropic s-wave BCS superconductivity.

The proposed local-distortion mechanism can be tested by cooling through the suspected transition while comparing low-temperature electronic and structural measurements with measurements above the transition.
Absence of a local structural change below the transition would falsify the proposed local-distortion mechanism.
Absence of a superconducting gap, or observation of pronounced gap anisotropy, would falsify the proposed conventional isotropic s-wave account.
